summary: Alteplase (recombinant tissue plasminogen activator, rt-PA) is a fibrinolytic that converts plasminogen to plasmin to dissolve fibrin clots. It is used for acute ischemic stroke (within 3 hours of symptom onset per label), acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction, and acute massive pulmonary embolism; a low-dose formulation (Cathflo Activase 2 mg) restores function to occluded central venous catheters. The dominant hazard is BLEEDING, including life-threatening and fatal intracranial hemorrhage. STRICT TIME WINDOWS and rigorous exclusion of contraindications (recent surgery/trauma, active bleeding, uncontrolled hypertension, intracranial lesions) are essential. It must be given by trained clinicians with intensive monitoring for hemorrhage and neurologic deterioration.
indications: Acute ischemic stroke - to improve neurologic recovery and reduce disability, started within 3 hours of symptom onset (label) after excluding intracranial hemorrhage by imaging
Acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) - to reduce mortality and improve ventricular function
Acute massive pulmonary embolism - in adults with obstruction of blood flow or hemodynamic instability
Restoration of function to central venous access devices occluded by clot (Cathflo Activase)

dosage.d: 0.9 mg/kg (maximum 90 mg); give 10% as IV bolus over 1 minute, then remainder as infusion over 60 minutes
dosage.n: Begin within 3 hours of symptom onset; exclude ICH on imaging first

dosage.d: 15 mg IV bolus, then 50 mg over next 30 minutes, then 35 mg over next 60 minutes
dosage.n: Total dose not to exceed 100 mg

dosage.d: 15 mg IV bolus, then 0.75 mg/kg over 30 minutes (not to exceed 50 mg), then 0.50 mg/kg over next 60 minutes (not to exceed 35 mg)
dosage.n: Total dose not to exceed 100 mg

dosage.d: 100 mg total: 60 mg in first hour (6-10 mg as bolus), then 20 mg over second hour, then 20 mg over third hour; for <65 kg use 1.25 mg/kg over 3 hours
100 mg as IV infusion over 2 hours
dosage.n: Institute heparin near end of or after infusion when aPTT/thrombin time <=2x normal

dosage.d: 2 mg in 2 mL instilled into the occluded catheter; if function not restored at 120 min, may instill a second 2 mg dose
dosage.n: For patients <=30 kg use 110% of internal lumen volume, max 2 mg; do not exceed 2 doses

admin: For IV use only; reconstitute with Sterile Water for Injection to 1 mg/mL (50 mg/100 mg vials) - do NOT use Bacteriostatic Water
Reconstitute gently (swirl, do not shake); use within 8 hours when stored at 2-30 C
Do not add other medications to or infuse other drugs through the same IV line
Use an infusion pump and a dedicated line; follow the bolus-then-infusion sequence exactly for the indication
Cathflo: instill into the occluded catheter only - do not infuse into the systemic circulation
Have resuscitation and bleeding-management resources immediately available during administration
moa: Alteplase is a recombinant tissue plasminogen activator that binds fibrin within a thrombus and converts entrapped plasminogen to plasmin. Plasmin degrades the fibrin matrix of the clot, producing local fibrinolysis and clot dissolution. Its relative fibrin specificity limits but does not eliminate systemic activation of circulating plasminogen, so systemic fibrinolysis and bleeding can still occur.

absolute: Recent (within 3 months) intracranial or intraspinal surgery, serious head trauma, or previous stroke (per indication)
Intracranial conditions that may increase bleeding risk - neoplasm, arteriovenous malformation, or aneurysm
For acute ischemic stroke: current intracranial hemorrhage, or suspicion of subarachnoid hemorrhage
Known hypersensitivity to alteplase or any component
relative: Recent major surgery, trauma, GI/GU bleeding, or arterial puncture at a noncompressible site
Advanced age, low body weight, or current anticoagulant/antiplatelet therapy
Acute pericarditis, subacute bacterial endocarditis, or hemostatic defects
Pregnancy, diabetic hemorrhagic retinopathy, or other conditions with bleeding hazard
For stroke: minor/rapidly improving deficits, seizure at onset, glucose <50 or >400 mg/dL, platelets <100,000
monitor: Signs of internal or intracranial bleeding (neurologic decline, severe headache, new hypertension)
Blood pressure - treat aggressively to keep within indication-specific limits
Puncture/access sites and gums/urine/stool for occult bleeding

preg: Limited human data. Alteplase does not cross the placenta appreciably (large molecule) but maternal bleeding, including at delivery, is a concern. Use only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus and mother.
lact: There is no information on the presence of alteplase in human milk or its effects on the breastfed infant. As a large protein it is unlikely to be absorbed intact by the infant; the short single-administration nature limits exposure. Consider benefits of breastfeeding against the mother's clinical need.
renal: No specific dosage adjustment is recommended in the labeling for renal impairment. Clinical judgment regarding overall bleeding risk applies.
hepatic: No specific dosage adjustment is recommended; alteplase is cleared primarily by the liver. Severe hepatic disease may increase bleeding risk through impaired coagulation factor synthesis - use with caution.

major: Heparin, warfarin, and other anticoagulants - markedly increased bleeding risk; time heparin per protocol
Antiplatelet agents (aspirin, clopidogrel, GP IIb/IIIa inhibitors) - increased risk of hemorrhage
ACE inhibitors - reports of increased risk of angioedema, especially with stroke use
moderate: Other thrombolytics or fibrinolytics - additive bleeding risk
Drugs that alter platelet function (e.g., dipyridamole) - increased bleeding
interactions.alcohol: Not applicable to a single acute administration.
interactions.diagnostics: Causes transient decreases in fibrinogen and plasminogen and increases in fibrin/fibrinogen degradation products; coagulation assays (PT, aPTT, fibrinogen) may be altered during and after therapy.

serious: Hypersensitivity / anaphylactoid reactions and angioedema (orolingual, especially with ACE inhibitors)
emergency: Intracranial hemorrhage - sudden severe headache, acute neurologic deterioration, new seizure, vomiting, or change in consciousness - STOP infusion immediately
Major uncontrolled hemorrhage with hemodynamic compromise
Anaphylaxis or orolingual angioedema compromising the airway

monitoring: Continuous monitoring for bleeding - neurologic checks for ICH, plus puncture sites, GI/GU tract, and gums
Blood pressure frequently; keep within indication-specific targets (e.g., <185/110 mmHg before and <180/105 mmHg after stroke thrombolysis)
Neurologic status (NIH Stroke Scale) at frequent intervals; obtain urgent CT if deterioration suggests ICH
Cardiac rhythm and hemodynamics in MI; signs of reperfusion arrhythmia
Coagulation parameters (fibrinogen, PT/aPTT, hematocrit/hemoglobin) as clinically indicated
counsel: This is an emergency clot-dissolving medicine given in hospital by trained staff
Report immediately any sudden severe headache, weakness, vision change, confusion, or trouble speaking - these may signal bleeding in the brain
Tell staff about any bleeding, bruising, blood in urine or stool, or black tarry stools
Avoid unnecessary movement, injections, and invasive procedures during and shortly after treatment to limit bleeding
Inform clinicians of all medications (especially blood thinners and aspirin) and any recent surgery, trauma, or bleeding problems
pk: Rapid fibrinolytic activity within minutes of administration
Plasma concentration peaks during/at end of infusion
Initial ~5 min; rapidly cleared (>50% cleared within ~5 min, ~80% within 10 min)
Short; coagulation effects (low fibrinogen) may persist for hours after the brief plasma presence
Store powder at 2-30 C (36-86 F), protected from excessive light; use reconstituted solution within 8 hours
pearls: BLEEDING is the principal hazard - intracranial hemorrhage can be fatal; STOP the infusion at once for any suspected ICH or major bleed
TIME IS BRAIN - acute ischemic stroke must be treated within 3 hours of onset (label) and only after CT/MRI excludes hemorrhage
Rigorously screen contraindications: active bleeding, recent surgery/trauma, intracranial lesions, severe uncontrolled hypertension
Aggressively control blood pressure before and during stroke thrombolysis to reduce ICH risk
Orolingual angioedema can occur, particularly in patients on ACE inhibitors - monitor the airway
Do not mix with other drugs or infuse through a shared line; reconstitute with Sterile Water (not Bacteriostatic Water)
missed: Not applicable. Alteplase is administered acutely by clinicians as a one-time, time-critical infusion in an emergency or procedural setting; there is no patient-managed dosing schedule, so the missed-dose concept does not apply.
overdose: There is no specific antidote. Overdose increases the risk of serious bleeding, including intracranial hemorrhage. Stop the infusion immediately; provide supportive care, replace blood volume and coagulation factors (cryoprecipitate/fibrinogen, fresh frozen plasma, platelets), and consider antifibrinolytic agents (e.g., aminocaproic acid) for severe uncontrolled bleeding. Manage acutely with urgent imaging and neurosurgical/hematology consultation as needed.
